label: Primeval history
note: Genesis 1-11. No external chronology applies; the start date is Ussher's, shown only to mark where the traditional reckoning begins.

label: Patriarchs
note: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph. Dates follow the biblical internal chronology; no external source names any of them.

label: Israel in Egypt
note: Length depends on whether Exod 12:40's 430 years is read as time in Egypt or from Abraham onward.

label: Exodus and wilderness
note: Shown at the late (13th-century) date. The early date derived from 1 Kgs 6:1 puts it at 1446 BCE; both hypotheses appear as separate events.

label: Conquest and judges
note: The Merneptah Stele (c. 1207) is the first external mention of Israel and falls inside this band.

label: United monarchy
note: Saul, David, Solomon. The Tel Dan Stele (c. 840) refers to the 'House of David', the earliest external trace of the dynasty.

label: Divided kingdom
note: Israel in the north, Judah in the south. Assyrian records fix several kings to the year.

label: Judah alone
note: From the fall of Samaria to the fall of Jerusalem.

label: Hellenistic period
note: Between the testaments. Daniel reaches its final form in this window; the Maccabean revolt falls at its centre.

label: Apostolic age
note: Every New Testament book is written inside this band; the letters of Paul are the earliest of them.
